Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG OPINION NO. 10 S. 2010 25 January 2010 GOVERNOR CARLITO S. MARQUEZ Provincial Capitol Building Kalibo, Aklan Dear Governor Marquez: This has reference to your earlier letter requesting for this Department's guidance relative to the expiration of the three (3)-month suspension imposed against Mayor Antonio T. Maming of Banga Aklan. Your letter was forwarded to this level by Regional Director Evelyn A. Trompeta, DILG-Region VI As culled from the records forwarded to this Department, hereunder are the antecedent facts: On 08 October 2009, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Aklan promulgated Resolution No. 2009-255, entitled "A Resolution Adopting the Majority Recommendation of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan Investigating Committee on SP Administrative Case No. 09-01 (Vicente R. Seraspi, Jr. vs. Antonio T. Maming) for Abuse of Authority, Misconduct in Office, and Neglect of Duty But the Imposable Penalty is Reduced to Three (3) Months Suspension Only"; The suspension order against Mayor Maming was served on 12 October 2009 and accordingly, on this date, Mayor Maming has also ceased to perform his duties and functions as Mayor of Banga, Aklan; Thereafter, Mayor Maming appealed the decision of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan before the Office of the President. Pending his appeal, Mayor Maming continued to serve his three(3)-month suspension; Meanwhile, the complainant in the aforecited case, Mr. Vicente R. Serapio, Jr. filed a pleading before the Office of the President in answer to the Appeal of Mayor Maming and further prayed therein for the extension of the penalty imposed by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan from three (3) months to six (6) months; On 17 December 2009, the Office of the President issued a Stay Order directing the re-assumption of Mayor Maming to his post as Mayor of Banga, Aklan; On 28 December 2009, you filed a Motion for Reconsideration assailing the Stay Order issued by the OP, which thus prevented DILG-Region VI Director Evelyn A. Trompeta from implementing the said Order;

-2- • To date, the Office of the President has yet to resolve the Appeal as well as the motion/pleading, which you and Mr. Serapio had previously filed before the Office of the President. In view of the foregoing, it is now your position that the aforesaid pending antecedents on the instant case be resolved first before the penalty of suspension imposed upon Mayor Maming is lifted for it creates legal questions if ever, granting arguendo, the appeal will be decided in favor of the complainant Serapio. At the outset, allow us first to point out the undisputed fact that while the Office of the President has issued a Stay Order directing the reassumption of Mayor Maming to his post, the Department, however, was not able to implement the same as it was returned to the Office of the President for clarification concerning legal issues. Accordingly, as borne by the facts on record, Mayor Maming started to serve his suspension on 12 October 2009 and completed the service of the same on 12 January 2010, without any interruption. Going now to the issue at hand, while we understand your apprehension in lifting the suspension on 13 January 2010 pending resolution of the appeai by the Office of the President, we cannot, however, avoid to counter-speculate a situation where what if the appeal of complainant Serapio will be denied or, as it also happens in some instances, the penalty of suspension will be reduced. In this regard, it bears to point out that If the appeal of complainant Serapio is dismissed or if the penalty of suspension against the Mayor is reduced, it would be at the height of great injustice if Mayor Maming will be burdened to still serve the suspension notwithstanding the fact that he has already completeiy served the original suspension of three (3) months decreed by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. This situation will also deprive the people of Banga, Aklan, of the services of their duly chosen Mayor in the last elections. Fairplay would, therefore, dictate that after completely serving the three (3) months penalty of suspension ordered by the Sangguniang Panlaiawigan, Mayor Maming should now be allowed to reassume his post as of 13 January 2010, which assumption, however, would be without prejudice to his serving of another period of suspension should the appeal of complainant Serapio be favorably granted by the Office of the President. We hope that we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, AUST EA. PANADE O Undersecretar copy furnished: Director Evelyn A. Trompeta DILG-Region VI Fort San Pedro, Iloilo City Legal:arb/17
